newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March retail sales fall 0.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Canada March retail sales fall 0.8 percent.

text.p: Canadian retail sales fell 0.8 percent in March to a seasonally adjusted C$18.88 billion from a revised C$19.03 billion (C$19.09 billion) in February, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a -0.8 +6.1 C$14.34 bln

Statistics Canada said early indications for April were for a rise in the number of employees in retail trade, up 0.6 percent. The number of housing starts in April declined 7.8 percent from the same period in 1996. Retail trade in the United States decreased 0.3 percent in April after no change in March.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.9 percent rise in retail sales in March after February's 1.1 percent rise.

Statistics Canada said that although consumers spent less in March, retail sales remained strong in the first quarter of 1997. Retail sales were up 2.6 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 and up 1.8 percent in the first quarter of 1997, the strongest back-to-back increases in quarterly sales since the last quarter of 1993 and the first quarter of 1994, StatsCan said.
In March, only general merchandise stores recorded sales increases, up 0.5 percent, due to advances by department stores, with sales up 0.8 percent, the federal agency said.

In terms of dollar values, the greatest decline in retail sales in March was in the automotive sector, down 1.2 percent, StatsCan said. The drop was evenly split among motor vehicle and recreational vehicle dealers, both down 0.9 percent, and automotive parts and accessories stores, down 3.8 percent.

Sales by food stores declined marginally in March, falling 0.2 percent, as the small increases in supermarkets and grocery stores were offset by declining sales in more specialized food stores, StatsCan said.
Regionally, Western Canada registered the strongest advances in retail sales in the first quarter of 1997, up 3.5 percent.
